title: AlphaCNOT exposed a shorter construction for remote qubit swaps
summary: Researchers found a recurring circuit in AlphaCNOT outputs and proved that two qubits at graph distance d greater than one can be swapped using at most 6d−4 CNOT gates. The corresponding construction that chains adjacent SWAPs uses 6d−3.
ai_technology: AlphaCNOT learned policy and value networks with Monte Carlo tree search
organization: University of Udine; University of Catania; University of Naples Federico II; National Institute for Astrophysics

source_review.scope: §§2–3, AlphaCNOT method and constructive theorem, primary PDF front matter

evidence.tested: AlphaCNOT revealed the pattern over multiple test topologies. The authors gave a constructive proof along a shortest path, valid for any distance in the stated coupling model.
evidence.unknown: The comparison is against the adjacent-SWAP construction. The bound does not establish CNOT optimality or measured hardware performance.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaCNOT’s learned policy and value networks guided a constrained circuit search. The authors recognized a recurring pattern and proved its general gate bound.
